blocks.p: With a controller, a mark shows what the controller is on. There are four marks to choose from. Figure 17-1 shows each of them on the same row of the *Character* window, the row for the apples, with the inventory shown as a list. The four are described in Table 17-1 on the facing page.

caption: Figure 17-1
Pointing hand, Corner marks, One wash and Marching ants, from the top.

blocks.p: The mark shows only while a controller is in use, and only in the window the controller is in. When you use the mouse, the mark clears; the next press on the controller brings it back where it was.

marks.text: Pointing hand, the default: a hand at the left of the row.
Corner marks: four brackets round the row.
One wash: the whole row fills with the accent.
Marching ants: a dashed outline round the row.

sticky.text: Four ways to mark what the controller is on.

blocks.p: The highlight is chosen in the window menu, under *Controller highlight*. It can also be chosen in *ZeD setup*, where a sample row beside the choice shows the mark, and on the ZeD wheel. The choice is saved with the other ZNIX settings.
To choose a highlight from the window menu:

list: Click the window box at the right end of the title bar.
Choose one of the four marks described in Table 17-1.

table.label: Table 17-1
table.title: The four highlights
head: Highlight
What it draws
rows: The default. A pointing hand at the left of the element, its fingertip on the element's left edge, over a light wash.
Four L-shaped marks just outside the corners of the element, in the accent color, over a light wash.
The whole element fills with the accent, and its words change to stay readable.
A dashed outline just outside the element, the dashes moving round it, over a light wash.

blocks.note: On an element that is already solid in the accent color, One wash draws a ring inside the element instead.
